en.name: Amaranth, whole grain
en.summary: Amaranth is a tiny whole seed cooked like a porridge grain, and it carries its germ and its oil intact. That oil is what limits it: about 4 months in a sealed container in the cupboard, and 8 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: Keep amaranth in an airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard and use it within about 4 months. That is short for something that looks as inert as a bag of seeds, and the reason is the germ: amaranth is a whole grain with a relatively high oil content, and oil turns rancid long before anything else goes wrong. Keep it away from the stove and out of the light, and buy the size of bag you will actually get through, not the economy sack.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for amaranth, so none is given here. The fridge is still a sensible halfway house for an opened bag in a hot, humid kitchen — cold slows the oil turning — but the jar must be genuinely airtight, because amaranth takes up fridge odours and moisture readily, and condensation on a cold jar brought out onto a warm counter is exactly what you do not want in a dry grain.
en.freezer: The freezer doubles it: about 8 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in an airtight container or a heavy freezer bag with the air pressed out. Freezing slows the oil oxidising and settles any question of pantry weevils in a bag brought home from a bulk bin. Let the container come back to room temperature before you open it, so moisture condenses on the outside rather than on the grain.
spoilage: A bitter, paint-like or crayon smell when you open the jar — rancid oil, and the usual end of amaranth.
A dusty, musty smell, or visible webbing and small moths in the jar.
Clumping or damp patches in what should be a free-running seed.
Cooked porridge that tastes bitter however you season it.
tips: Buy small bags; four months passes before a big sack is half used.
Smell it before you cook it — rancidity is not visible.
Freeze the surplus on the day you buy it rather than after it has sat out.
Label the jar with the purchase date, not the packet date.

faq.q: How long does amaranth keep in the cupboard?
faq.a: About 4 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark place. It is a whole grain with oil in the germ, so it does not keep like white rice.
Yes, about 8 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in an airtight container. It also deals with any pantry insects.

faq.q: How can you tell if amaranth has gone off?
faq.a: By smell. Rancid grain smells bitter or faintly of paint, and it will make the finished dish taste bitter too.

zh.name: 莧籽
zh.summary: 莧籽是像穀物一樣煮成粥的細小全穀種子，胚芽和油脂都完整保留。限制它的正是那些油脂：密封放櫥櫃約 4 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 8 個月。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐，放在陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，約 4 個月內用完。對一袋看起來毫無動靜的種子來說這算短，原因就在胚芽：莧籽是含油量偏高的全穀，而油脂走油耗，遠比其他問題早發生。請遠離爐火與光線，並且買你真的吃得完的份量，不要買大包裝。
zh.fridge: 莧籽沒有公布的冷藏期限，所以這裡也不給。不過在濕熱的廚房裡，開封後的袋子放冰箱仍是合理的折衷——低溫能延緩油脂氧化——但罐子必須真的密封，因為莧籽很會吸冰箱的氣味和濕氣，而冰冷的罐子拿到溫暖檯面上結露，正是乾燥穀物最怕的事。
zh.freezer: 冷凍可以讓時間加倍：−18 °C 下約 8 個月，裝密封容器或厚冷凍袋並壓出空氣。冷凍能延緩油脂氧化，也順便解決散裝買回來可能帶著的米蟲問題。要開封前先讓容器回到室溫，讓水氣凝在容器外面而不是穀粒上。
spoilage: 打開罐子聞到苦味、油漆味或蠟筆味——那是油脂走油耗，也是莧籽最常見的結局。
有灰塵般的霉味，或罐內看到絲網和小蛾。
本該粒粒分明卻結塊或有受潮的區塊。
煮成的粥不管怎麼調味都帶苦味。
tips: 買小包；四個月一到，大包裝往往還沒用到一半。
下鍋前先聞一下——油耗是看不出來的。
要冷凍就買回來當天凍，不要放了一陣子才凍。
在罐子上標「購買日期」而不是包裝上的製造日期。

faq.q: 莧籽放櫥櫃可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封罐、陰涼避光，約 4 個月。它是帶胚芽油脂的全穀，不像白米那麼耐放。
可以，−18 °C 下密封容器約 8 個月，順便解決米蟲問題。
靠聞的。走油耗的穀物聞起來發苦或有淡淡的油漆味，煮出來的東西也會苦。
